// ============================================================================
// MODULE: hdmi_top
// DESCRIPTION: Configurable top-level for HDMI output.
// CLOCK NOTE: Based on the board clock, requires a clk_pixel and a clk_tmds(= 5*clk_pixel)
// On the Tang Nano 9K, these clocks must be generated by an rPLL module.
// ============================================================================

module hdmi_top #( 
    // Horizontal parameters (Pixel)   | ACTIVE | FRONT | SYNC | BACK |
    parameter int H_ACTIVE   = 640,  
    parameter int H_FRONT    = 16, 
    parameter int H_SYNC     = 96,
    parameter int H_BACK     = 48,
    parameter int H_TOTAL = H_ACTIVE + H_FRONT + H_SYNC + H_BACK,   //800

    // Vertical Parameters (Lines)     | ACTIVE | FRONT | SYNC | BACK |    
    parameter int V_ACTIVE   = 480,
    parameter int V_FRONT    = 10,
    parameter int V_SYNC     = 2,
    parameter int V_BACK     = 33,
    parameter int V_TOTAL = V_ACTIVE + V_FRONT + V_SYNC + V_BACK,   //525

    // Polarity
    parameter bit H_SYNC_POL = 1'b0,
    parameter bit V_SYNC_POL = 1'b0,

    // Needed bits to correct count pixels
    parameter int H_BITS = $clog2(H_TOTAL),
    parameter int V_BITS = $clog2(V_TOTAL),

    //Thermal parameters for conversion
    parameter int TEMP_MIN   = 16'd27315,
    parameter int unsigned TEMP_SHIFT = 3
)(
    input  logic rst_n,       // Asynchronous reset active low
    input  logic clk_27MHz,   // Board clock
   
    
    // VIGIL80 input signals
    input  logic vigil_sck,
    input  logic vigil_csb,
    input  logic vigil_mosi,
    
    // Differential outputs (On the Tang Nano these are mapped to the TLVDS/LVCMOS33 pins)
    output logic tmds_clk_p,  output logic tmds_clk_n,
    output logic tmds_d0_p,   output logic tmds_d0_n,  // Blue
    output logic tmds_d1_p,   output logic tmds_d1_n,  // Green
    output logic tmds_d2_p,   output logic tmds_d2_n   // Red
);

    // --- Internal signals ---
    logic clk_pixel;          // Pixel_clk
    logic clk_tmds;           // TMDS clock 5x 
    logic [H_BITS-1:0] cx;    //counter x
    logic [V_BITS-1:0] cy;    //counter y
    logic hsync, vsync, vde;
    logic [7:0] red, green, blue;
    logic [9:0] tmds_r, tmds_g, tmds_b;
    

    logic [12:0] ir_rd_addr;
    logic [7:0]  ir_rd_pixel;
    logic        ir_rd_req;
    logic        ir_rd_valid;

    logic        hdmi_frame_start;
    logic        ir_frame_available;
    logic        ir_writing_allowed;

    assign hdmi_frame_start = (cx == '0) && (cy == '0);  //is the rd_swap_point

    // --- Clock stage ---
    Gowin_rPLL PLL(
        .clkout(clk_tmds),  //fast clock for serializer
        .reset(~rst_n),
        .clkin(clk_27MHz)
    );

    CLKDIV #(
    .DIV_MODE("5"),
    .GSREN("false")
    ) clk_div_5 (
    .CLKOUT(clk_pixel),   //pixel clock
    .HCLKIN(clk_tmds),
    .RESETN(rst_n),
    .CALIB(1'b0)
    );


// 1. Sincronisms Generator (Timings)    
video_timing #(
        .H_ACTIVE   (H_ACTIVE),
        .H_FRONT    (H_FRONT),
        .H_SYNC     (H_SYNC),
        .H_BACK     (H_BACK),
        .H_TOTAL    (H_TOTAL),
        .H_SYNC_POL (H_SYNC_POL),
        .H_BITS     (H_BITS),

        .V_ACTIVE   (V_ACTIVE),
        .V_FRONT    (V_FRONT),
        .V_SYNC     (V_SYNC),
        .V_BACK     (V_BACK),
        .V_TOTAL    (V_TOTAL),
        .V_SYNC_POL (V_SYNC_POL),
        .V_BITS     (V_BITS)
    ) timing_inst (
        .clk   (clk_pixel),
        .rst_n (rst_n),
        .cx    (cx),
        .cy    (cy),
        .hsync (hsync),
        .vsync (vsync),
        .vde   (vde)
    );


// ============================================================================
// 2. IR camera manager
// ============================================================================

vigil80_ir_manager #(
    .IMG_W         (80),
    .IMG_H         (80),
    .FRAME_PIX     (6400),
    .FOOTER_WORDS  (23),
    .TOTAL_WORDS   (6423),
    .ADDR_BITS     (13),

    .TEMP_MIN      (TEMP_MIN),
    .TEMP_SHIFT    (TEMP_SHIFT)
) vigil80_manager_inst (
    .rst_n          (rst_n),

    .vigil_sck      (vigil_sck),
    .vigil_csb      (vigil_csb),
    .vigil_mosi     (vigil_mosi),

    .rd_clk         (clk_pixel),
    .rd_swap_point  (hdmi_frame_start),
    .rd_req         (ir_rd_req),
    .rd_addr        (ir_rd_addr),

    .rd_pixel       (ir_rd_pixel),
    .rd_valid       (ir_rd_valid),

    .frame_available(ir_frame_available),
    .writing_allowed(ir_writing_allowed)
);

// ============================================================================
// IR image renderer
// ============================================================================

thermal_hdmi_renderer #(
    .H_ACTIVE  (H_ACTIVE),
    .V_ACTIVE  (V_ACTIVE),
    .H_BITS    (H_BITS),
    .V_BITS    (V_BITS),

    .IMG_W     (80),
    .IMG_H     (80),
    .SCALE     (6),
     
    .FRAME_PIX (6400),
    .ADDR_BITS (13)
) thermal_renderer_inst (
    .clk_pixel (clk_pixel),
    .rst_n     (rst_n),

    .cx        (cx),
    .cy        (cy),
    .vde       (vde),

    .rd_req    (ir_rd_req),
    .rd_addr   (ir_rd_addr),
    .rd_pixel  (ir_rd_pixel),
    .rd_valid  (ir_rd_valid),

    .red       (red),
    .green     (green),
    .blue      (blue)
);

// =========================================================================
// 3. TMDS ENCODER + SERIALIZER
// =========================================================================

    // --- Pipeline alignment delay (2 cycles) ---
    logic [1:0] hsync_d, vsync_d, vde_d_top;

    always_ff @(posedge clk_pixel or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        hsync_d   <= 2'b00;
        vsync_d   <= 2'b00;
        vde_d_top <= 2'b00;
    end
    else begin
        hsync_d   <= {hsync_d[0], hsync};
        vsync_d   <= {vsync_d[0], vsync};
        vde_d_top <= {vde_d_top[0], vde};
    end
    end

    //Encoder TMDS (3 channels)
    // The BLU channel (D0) carries HSYNC and VSYNC during blanking (vde=0)
    
    tmds_encoder enc_b (
        .clk      (clk_pixel),
        .rst_n    (rst_n),
        .data_in  (blue),
        .ctrl     ({vsync_d[1], hsync_d[1]}),
        .vde      (vde_d_top[1]),
        .tmds_out (tmds_b)
    );

        tmds_encoder enc_g (
        .clk      (clk_pixel),
        .rst_n    (rst_n),
        .data_in  (green),
        .ctrl     (2'b00),
        .vde      (vde_d_top[1]),
        .tmds_out (tmds_g)
    );

        tmds_encoder enc_r (
        .clk      (clk_pixel),
        .rst_n    (rst_n),
        .data_in  (red),
        .ctrl     (2'b00),
        .vde      (vde_d_top[1]),
        .tmds_out (tmds_r)
    );

    // Serializer 10:1 (Serialization of the clock needed to compensate the delays introduced by the serialiser)
    logic s_clk, s_d0, s_d1, s_d2;

    serializer_10to1 ser_b   (.rst_n(rst_n), .clk_pixel(clk_pixel), .clk_tmds(clk_tmds), .data_in(tmds_b),     .serial_out(s_d0));
    serializer_10to1 ser_g   (.rst_n(rst_n), .clk_pixel(clk_pixel), .clk_tmds(clk_tmds), .data_in(tmds_g),     .serial_out(s_d1));
    serializer_10to1 ser_r   (.rst_n(rst_n), .clk_pixel(clk_pixel), .clk_tmds(clk_tmds), .data_in(tmds_r),     .serial_out(s_d2));
    serializer_10to1 ser_clk (.rst_n(rst_n), .clk_pixel(clk_pixel), .clk_tmds(clk_tmds), .data_in(10'b1111100000), .serial_out(s_clk));

    // The ELVDS_OBUF primitive is required to generate real differential hardware
    ELVDS_OBUF obuf_d0 (
    .I (s_d0),
    .O (tmds_d0_p),
    .OB(tmds_d0_n)
    );

    ELVDS_OBUF obuf_d1 (
    .I (s_d1),
    .O (tmds_d1_p),
    .OB(tmds_d1_n)
    );

    ELVDS_OBUF obuf_d2 (
    .I (s_d2),
    .O (tmds_d2_p),
    .OB(tmds_d2_n)
    );

    ELVDS_OBUF obuf_clk (
    .I (s_clk),
    .O (tmds_clk_p),
    .OB(tmds_clk_n)
    );

endmodule

// ============================================================================
// MODULE: double_framebuffer_gowin_sdp
// DESCRIPTION: Double framebuffer using two Gowin_SDP RAM IPs.
//
// RAM0 and RAM1 are used as ping-pong buffers.
// The buffer swap is performed only at rd_swap_point.
//
// Write side:
// - clocked by VIGIL80 video_sck or OV5640 ov_pclk;
// - writes incoming camera pixels;
// - writes only complete frames into the selected bank.
//
// Read side:
// - clocked by HDMI clk_pixel;
// - provides pixels to the HDMI renderer;
// - changes the displayed bank only at the start of an HDMI frame.
//
// IMPORTANT:
// Gowin_SDP RAM has synchronous read access.
// After a read request, rd_data becomes available one rd_clk cycle later.
// rd_valid indicates when the output data is valid.
//
// A single toggle signal, completed_toggle_wr, crosses from the camera clock
// domain to the HDMI clock domain.
// The toggle has two meanings:
// - a change in value indicates that a new complete frame is available;
// - the current value identifies the framebuffer that has been completed..
// ============================================================================
module double_framebuffer_gowin_sdp #(
    parameter int FRAME_PIX = 6400,
    parameter int ADDR_BITS = $clog2(FRAME_PIX)
)(
    input  logic rst_n,

    // ========================================================================
    // Write side - camera domain
    // ========================================================================

    input  logic                 wr_clk,       // Clock generated by the camera
    input  logic                 wr_valid,     // High when one pixel must be written
    input  logic [ADDR_BITS-1:0] wr_addr,      // Address of the camera pixel
    input  logic [7:0]           wr_data,      // RGB332 pixel
    input  logic                 wr_frame_done,// High when a complete frame has been received

    output logic                 wr_allow,     // Permission sent to camera capture:
                                               // 1: next frame can be stored
                                               // 0: incoming frame must be discarded
                                               // because the available bank is still
                                               // displayed by HDMI

    // ========================================================================
    // Read side - HDMI domain
    // ========================================================================

    input  logic                 rd_clk,        // HDMI pixel clock
    input  logic                 rd_swap_point, // High at the start of an HDMI frame
    input  logic                 rd_req,        // Pixel read request
    input  logic [ADDR_BITS-1:0] rd_addr,       // Pixel address requested by HDMI

    output logic [7:0]           rd_data,       // RGB332 pixel read from RAM
    output logic                 rd_valid,      // High when rd_data is valid

    output logic                 frame_available
                                                // Debug/status signal:
                                                // high after the first complete
                                                // camera frame has arrived
);

    // ========================================================================
    // Bank control
    // ========================================================================

    logic wr_bank; // Buffer currently written by the camera:
                   // 0: write RAM0
                   // 1: write RAM1

    logic rd_bank; // Buffer currently read by HDMI:
                   // 0: read RAM0
                   // 1: read RAM1

    // At reset:
    // - HDMI reads RAM0;
    // - camera writes RAM1.
    //
    // This avoids a read/write collision immediately after reset.

    // completed_toggle_wr is updated after every complete camera frame.
    //
    // The signal performs two functions:
    // 1. a change in its value signals a newly completed frame;
    // 2. its value identifies the completed framebuffer.
    //
    // RAM1 complete -> completed_toggle_wr = 1
    // RAM0 complete -> completed_toggle_wr = 0

    logic completed_toggle_wr;

    // ========================================================================
    // Synchronize rd_bank from HDMI/read clock domain to camera/write domain
    // ========================================================================
    //
    // rd_bank is generated in the rd_clk domain but is used in the wr_clk
    // domain to calculate wr_allow.
    //
    // Since rd_clk and wr_clk are asynchronous, rd_bank may change close to
    // a wr_clk edge and violate the setup/hold time of the first flip-flop.
    //
    // The two flip-flop synchronizer provides a stable copy of rd_bank in the
    // camera clock domain:
    //
    // rd_bank -> rd_bank_wr_meta -> rd_bank_wr_sync
    // ========================================================================

    logic rd_bank_wr_meta; // First synchronizer FF, may become metastable
    logic rd_bank_wr_sync; // Second synchronizer FF, safe in wr_clk domain

    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            rd_bank_wr_meta <= 1'b0;
            rd_bank_wr_sync <= 1'b0;
        end
        else begin
            rd_bank_wr_meta <= rd_bank;
            rd_bank_wr_sync <= rd_bank_wr_meta;
        end
    end

    // The camera may write only if the selected write bank is not the bank
    // currently displayed by HDMI.
    assign wr_allow = (wr_bank != rd_bank_wr_sync);

    // ========================================================================
    // Write-side bank update
    // ========================================================================
    //
    // wr_bank changes only after a complete frame has been written.
    //
    // completed_toggle_wr receives the value of the bank that has just been
    // completed. Therefore the signal identifies the completed bank and also
    // changes value at every valid frame completion.
    //
    // After completing one framebuffer, the camera selects the other bank.
    // If the other bank is still displayed by HDMI, wr_allow becomes zero and
    // the capture module discards incoming frames until HDMI releases it.
    // ========================================================================

    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wr_bank             <= 1'b1; // After reset, write RAM1
            completed_toggle_wr <= 1'b0;
        end
        else if (wr_frame_done && wr_allow) begin

            // wr_bank identifies the bank that has just been completed.
            //
            // Assigning wr_bank to completed_toggle_wr:
            // - signals the arrival of a complete frame;
            // - transfers the completed bank identifier to the read domain.
            completed_toggle_wr <= wr_bank;

            // Select the other framebuffer for the next writable frame.
            wr_bank <= ~wr_bank;
        end
    end

    // ========================================================================
    // Synchronize completed-frame event into HDMI/read clock domain
    // ========================================================================
    //
    // completed_toggle_wr is asynchronous with respect to rd_clk.
    // Two flip-flops synchronize the toggle into the HDMI clock domain:
    //
    // completed_toggle_wr
    //        ->
    // completed_toggle_rd_meta
    //        ->
    // completed_toggle_rd_sync
    //
    // A complete frame is detected when completed_toggle_rd_sync differs from
    // completed_toggle_rd_last.
    // ========================================================================

    logic completed_toggle_rd_meta;
    logic completed_toggle_rd_sync;
    logic completed_toggle_rd_last;

    // Indicates that one complete framebuffer is ready to be displayed,
    // but the swap is pending because HDMI is still displaying the current
    // framebuffer.
    logic pending_valid_rd;

    // Identifies which framebuffer is ready to be displayed.
    logic pending_bank_rd;

    always_ff @(posedge rd_clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            completed_toggle_rd_meta <= 1'b0;
            completed_toggle_rd_sync <= 1'b0;
            completed_toggle_rd_last <= 1'b0;

            pending_valid_rd <= 1'b0;
            pending_bank_rd  <= 1'b0;

            rd_bank         <= 1'b0; // After reset, read RAM0
            frame_available <= 1'b0;
        end
        else begin

            // Two-step synchronization of the completed-frame toggle.
            completed_toggle_rd_meta <= completed_toggle_wr;
            completed_toggle_rd_sync <= completed_toggle_rd_meta;

            // Swap the displayed framebuffer only at the beginning of an HDMI
            // frame and only if a complete camera frame is pending.
            //
            // This prevents tearing because rd_bank never changes in the middle
            // of an HDMI frame.
            if (rd_swap_point && pending_valid_rd) begin
                rd_bank          <= pending_bank_rd;
                pending_valid_rd <= 1'b0;
            end

            // Detect a newly completed camera frame.
            // The synchronized toggle value is also the completed bank number.
            //
            // This block is intentionally placed after the swap block.
            // If a swap and a new completed frame occur during the same rd_clk
            // cycle, the older pending frame is displayed and the newly
            // completed frame remains pending for the next HDMI frame.
            if (completed_toggle_rd_sync != completed_toggle_rd_last) begin
                completed_toggle_rd_last <= completed_toggle_rd_sync;

                pending_bank_rd  <= completed_toggle_rd_sync;
                pending_valid_rd <= 1'b1;

                // Status signal: once a complete frame has arrived,
                // frame_available remains high until reset.
                frame_available <= 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    // ========================================================================
    // RAM write and read enables
    // ========================================================================

    logic ram0_wr_en;
    logic ram1_wr_en;
    logic ram0_rd_en;
    logic ram1_rd_en;

    // The capture module samples wr_allow at the beginning of a camera frame
    // and generates wr_valid only when that complete frame is authorized.
    //
    // Therefore the RAM write enables depend on wr_valid and wr_bank.
    // wr_allow is not checked again for every pixel, avoiding interruption of
    // an already authorized frame if rd_bank changes asynchronously.
    assign ram0_wr_en = wr_valid && (wr_bank == 1'b0);
    assign ram1_wr_en = wr_valid && (wr_bank == 1'b1);

    // Only the framebuffer selected by rd_bank receives the HDMI read request.
    assign ram0_rd_en = rd_req && (rd_bank == 1'b0);
    assign ram1_rd_en = rd_req && (rd_bank == 1'b1);

    // ========================================================================
    // RAM outputs
    // ========================================================================

    logic [7:0] ram0_dout;
    logic [7:0] ram1_dout;

    // Gowin_SDP read output is synchronous.
    //
    // The selected bank and the read-request signal are delayed by one rd_clk
    // cycle so they remain aligned with the corresponding RAM output.
    logic rd_bank_d;
    logic rd_req_d;

    always_ff @(posedge rd_clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            rd_bank_d <= 1'b0;
            rd_req_d  <= 1'b0;
        end
        else begin
            // If a pixel is requested during the current cycle, the output
            // becomes valid during the next rd_clk cycle.
            rd_req_d <= rd_req;

            // Record which RAM was selected for the current read request.
            // The delayed value selects the correct synchronous RAM output.
            if (rd_req) begin
                rd_bank_d <= rd_bank;
            end
        end
    end

    // rd_valid is asserted one cycle after rd_req.
    assign rd_valid = rd_req_d;

    // Select the RAM output corresponding to the delayed read-bank value.
    always_comb begin
        if (rd_bank_d == 1'b0)
            rd_data = ram0_dout;
        else
            rd_data = ram1_dout;
    end

    // ========================================================================
    // Gowin SDP RAM 0
    //
    // Port A: camera write port
    // Port B: HDMI read port
    // ========================================================================

    Gowin_SDP ram0 (
        .dout   (ram0_dout),     // Output [7:0]

        // Write port
        .clka   (wr_clk),
        .cea    (ram0_wr_en),
        .reseta (~rst_n),        // RAM reset active high
        .ada    (wr_addr),
        .din    (wr_data),

        // Read port
        .clkb   (rd_clk),
        .ceb    (ram0_rd_en),
        .resetb (~rst_n),        // RAM reset active high
        .oce    (1'b1),
        .adb    (rd_addr)
    );

    // ========================================================================
    // Gowin SDP RAM 1
    //
    // Port A: camera write port
    // Port B: HDMI read port
    // ========================================================================

    Gowin_SDP ram1 (
        .dout   (ram1_dout),     // Output [7:0]

        // Write port
        .clka   (wr_clk),
        .cea    (ram1_wr_en),
        .reseta (~rst_n),        // RAM reset active high
        .ada    (wr_addr),
        .din    (wr_data),

        // Read port
        .clkb   (rd_clk),
        .ceb    (ram1_rd_en),
        .resetb (~rst_n),        // RAM reset active high
        .oce    (1'b1),
        .adb    (rd_addr)
    );

endmodule

// ============================================================================
// MODULE: serializer_10to1 (High-speed shift register)
// ============================================================================
module serializer_10to1 (
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic clk_pixel,
    input  logic clk_tmds,
    input  logic [9:0] data_in,
    output logic serial_out
);

    OSER10 serializer (
    .Q(serial_out),     //Serial output connected to the physical HDMI pin
    .D0(data_in[0]),    // Parallel bits coming from the TMDS encoder...
    .D1(data_in[1]),
    .D2(data_in[2]),
    .D3(data_in[3]),
    .D4(data_in[4]),
    .D5(data_in[5]),
    .D6(data_in[6]),
    .D7(data_in[7]),
    .D8(data_in[8]),
    .D9(data_in[9]),
    .PCLK(clk_pixel),   // pixel clock
    .FCLK(clk_tmds),    // TMDS clock (= pixel clk x 5)
    .RESET(~rst_n)      // The OSER10 has a HIGH-active reset
     );

endmodule


// ============================================================================
// MODULE: tmds_encoder pipelined (Algorithm 8b/10b for DVI/HDMI)
// ============================================================================
module tmds_encoder (
    input  logic        clk,
    input  logic        rst_n,

    input  logic        vde,        // data enable (1 = video, 0 = control)
    input  logic [1:0]  ctrl,       // {vsync, hsync}
    input  logic [7:0]  data_in,    // pixel data

    output logic [9:0]  tmds_out
);

    // Running disparity (signed)
    logic signed [5:0] disparity;   

    // Stage 1 signals
    logic [8:0] q_m_comb;
    logic [3:0] n1_data;
    logic       use_xnor;

    // Pipeline register between Stage 1 and Stage 2
    logic [8:0] q_m_pipe;
    logic       vde_pipe;
    logic [1:0] ctrl_pipe;

    // Stage 2 signals
    logic [3:0]        n1_qm;
    logic signed [5:0] balance;

    logic [9:0]        next_tmds;
    logic signed [5:0] next_disparity;

    // ===================================
    // COUNT ONES FUNCTION
    // ===================================
    function automatic [3:0] count_ones(input logic [7:0] x);
        begin
            count_ones = 4'd0;
            count_ones = {3'b000, x[0]} + {3'b000, x[1]} +
                {3'b000, x[2]} + {3'b000, x[3]} +
                {3'b000, x[4]} + {3'b000, x[5]} +
                {3'b000, x[6]} + {3'b000, x[7]};
        end
    endfunction

    //=========================================================
    // STAGE 1: Transition minimization (8b → 9b)
    //=========================================================

    always_comb begin
        n1_data = count_ones(data_in);

        // decision XOR / XNOR
        use_xnor = (n1_data > 4'd4) || ((n1_data == 4'd4) && (data_in[0] == 1'b0));

        // build q_m
        q_m_comb[0] = data_in[0];

        for (int i = 1; i < 8; i++) begin
            if (use_xnor)
                q_m_comb[i] = q_m_comb[i-1] ~^ data_in[i];
            else
                q_m_comb[i] = q_m_comb[i-1] ^  data_in[i];
        end

        // flag bit: 1 for XOR, 0 for XNOR
        q_m_comb[8] = ~use_xnor;   // use_xnor? 1'b0 : 1'b1
    end

    // =========================================================
    // PIPELINE REGISTER
    // =========================================================
    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            q_m_pipe  <= 9'd0;
            vde_pipe  <= 1'b0;
            ctrl_pipe <= 2'b00;
        end
        else begin
            q_m_pipe  <= q_m_comb;
            vde_pipe  <= vde;
            ctrl_pipe <= ctrl;
        end
    end

    // =========================================================
    // STAGE 2: DC balancing (9b → 10b)
    // ========================================================= 

    always_comb begin
        n1_qm = count_ones(q_m_pipe[7:0]);
        // Balance= disparity of current data : (N1 - N0) = n1_qm - (8 - n1_qm) = 2*n1_qm - 8
        balance = ($signed({2'b00,n1_qm}) << 1) - 6'sd8;    //$ for casting n1_qm to signed
    end

    // =========================================================
    // COMBINATIONAL NEXT CALCULATION (Uses pipelined vde/ctrl/q_m)
    // =========================================================

    always_comb begin
        // DEFAULT: to avoid latch
        next_tmds      = 10'b1101010100;  //default state
        next_disparity = disparity; 

        // LOGICA DECISIONALE
        if (!vde_pipe) begin
            // -- Modalità Blanking --
            next_disparity = 6'sd0;
            case (ctrl_pipe)
                2'b00:   next_tmds = 10'b1101010100;
                2'b01:   next_tmds = 10'b0010101011;
                2'b10:   next_tmds = 10'b0101010100;
                2'b11:   next_tmds = 10'b1010101011;
                default: next_tmds = 10'b1101010100;
            endcase
        end 
        else begin
            // -- Video Mode--
            if ((disparity == 6'sd0) || (balance == 6'sd0)) begin
                next_tmds[9]   = ~q_m_pipe[8];        //The two header bits must different for the std HDMI to avoid imbalance issues
                next_tmds[8]   =  q_m_pipe[8];
                next_tmds[7:0] =  q_m_pipe[8] ? q_m_pipe[7:0] : ~q_m_pipe[7:0];    // if q_m[8]=0 => next[9]=1 => reverse the data

                if (q_m_pipe[8] == 1'b0)
                    next_disparity = disparity - balance;
                else
                    next_disparity = disparity + balance;
            end
            else if ((disparity > 6'sd0 && balance > 6'sd0) ||
                     (disparity < 6'sd0 && balance < 6'sd0)) begin       //the disparity will get even worse => the data must be reversed

                next_tmds[9]   = 1'b1;
                next_tmds[8]   = q_m_pipe[8];
                next_tmds[7:0] = ~q_m_pipe[7:0];

                next_disparity = disparity + (q_m_pipe[8] ? 6'sd2 : 6'sd0) - balance;  //the condition takes into account the header bits disparity
            end
            else begin
                next_tmds[9]   = 1'b0;
                next_tmds[8]   = q_m_pipe[8];
                next_tmds[7:0] = q_m_pipe[7:0];

                next_disparity = disparity - (q_m_pipe[8] ? 6'sd0 : 6'sd2) + balance;
            end

        end
    end

    // =========================================================
    // OUTPUT REGISTER (only Flip-Flop)
    // =========================================================

    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            disparity <= 6'sd0;
            tmds_out  <= 10'b1101010100;
        end
        else begin
            disparity <= next_disparity;
            tmds_out  <= next_tmds;
        end
    end    

endmodule

// ============================================================================
// MODULE: video_timing
// ============================================================================
module video_timing #(
    //default values
    parameter int H_ACTIVE   = 320,  
    parameter int H_FRONT    = 16,
    parameter int H_SYNC     = 48,
    parameter int H_BACK     = 16,

    parameter int V_ACTIVE   = 240,
    parameter int V_FRONT    = 10,
    parameter int V_SYNC     = 2,
    parameter int V_BACK     = 10,

    parameter int H_TOTAL = H_ACTIVE + H_FRONT + H_SYNC + H_BACK,
    parameter int V_TOTAL = V_ACTIVE + V_FRONT + V_SYNC + V_BACK,

    parameter bit H_SYNC_POL = 1'b0,
    parameter bit V_SYNC_POL = 1'b0,

    parameter int H_BITS = $clog2(H_TOTAL),
    parameter int V_BITS = $clog2(V_TOTAL)
)(
    input  logic clk, rst_n,
    output logic [H_BITS-1:0] cx,   //counter x
    output logic [V_BITS-1:0] cy,   //counter y
    output logic hsync, vsync, vde
);

    //internal signals
    logic hsync_int, vsync_int;

    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            cx <= '0; cy <= '0;
        end 
        else begin
            if (cx == H_TOTAL - 1) begin
                cx <= '0;
                cy <= (cy == V_TOTAL - 1) ? '0 : cy + 1'b1;
            end 
            else begin
                cx <= cx + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    // logic to decide when activate sync signals
    assign hsync_int  = (cx >= H_ACTIVE + H_FRONT) && (cx < H_ACTIVE + H_FRONT + H_SYNC);  
    assign vsync_int = (cy >= V_ACTIVE + V_FRONT) && (cy < V_ACTIVE + V_FRONT + V_SYNC);  

    //polarity depends on resolution
    assign hsync = H_SYNC_POL ? hsync_int : ~hsync_int;     //when next row
    assign vsync = V_SYNC_POL ? vsync_int : ~vsync_int;     //when next frame
    assign vde   = (cx < H_ACTIVE) && (cy < V_ACTIVE);      // Video Data Enable
endmodule


// ============================================================================
// MODULE: vigil80_ir_manager
// DESCRIPTION:
// Top-level manager for VIGIL80 infrared camera.
//
// It includes:
// - SPI data reception from VIGIL80
// - 16-bit thermal pixel to 8-bit grayscale conversion
// - double framebuffer logic
// - two Gowin_SDP RAM instances
// - read interface for HDMI renderer
//
// VIGIL80 frame:
// - 80 x 80 active pixels = 6400 pixels
// - 23 footer words are discarded
// ============================================================================

module vigil80_ir_manager #(
    parameter int IMG_W         = 80,
    parameter int IMG_H         = 80,
    parameter int FRAME_PIX     = IMG_W * IMG_H,      // 6400
    parameter int FOOTER_WORDS  = 23,
    parameter int TOTAL_WORDS   = FRAME_PIX + FOOTER_WORDS,

    // Gowin_SDP IP configured as 6400 x 8, address [12:0]
    //parameter int RAM_ADDR_BITS = $clog2(FRAME_PIX),  //dipende dal numero di pixel real
    parameter int ADDR_BITS     = $clog2(FRAME_PIX),      //non utile

    // Thermal conversion parameters
    // TEMP_MIN = 27315 means about 0 degC in Kelvin x100
    parameter int TEMP_MIN      = 16'd27315,   //Minimum Temp used as reference for conversion
    parameter int unsigned TEMP_SHIFT    = 5
)(
    input  logic rst_n,

    // ========================================================================
    // VIGIL80 physical SPI-like video interface
    // Camera is SPI master
    // ========================================================================
    input  logic vigil_sck,  //clock camera IR (4.6 Mbits/s)
    input  logic vigil_csb,  //chip select active low
    input  logic vigil_mosi, //data 

    // ========================================================================
    // HDMI/read side
    // ========================================================================
    input  logic rd_clk,            // pixel clock
    input  logic rd_swap_point,     // usually HDMI frame start: cx==0 && cy==0
    input  logic rd_req,
    input  logic [ADDR_BITS-1:0] rd_addr,

    output logic [7:0] rd_pixel,
    output logic rd_valid,

    // ========================================================================
    // Optional debug/status outputs
    // ========================================================================
    output logic frame_available,
    output logic writing_allowed
);

    // ========================================================================
    // Internal write-side signals from SPI receiver to double framebuffer
    // ========================================================================

    logic [ADDR_BITS-1:0] wr_addr;
    logic [7:0] wr_data;         //converted 8 bit data
    logic       wr_valid;        //high when the data is converted in 8 bit and is ready to be memorized
    logic       wr_frame_done;   //high when the full frame just received can be saved in memory
    logic       wr_allow;        //used to not overwrite the frame that HDMI is reading ( 1: save frame; 0: discard frame )

    assign writing_allowed = wr_allow;

    // ========================================================================
    // 1. VIGIL80 SPI receiver + 16-bit to 8-bit conversion
    // ========================================================================

    vigil80_spi_receiver_16to8 #(
        .FRAME_PIX     (FRAME_PIX),
        .FOOTER_WORDS  (FOOTER_WORDS),
        .TOTAL_WORDS   (TOTAL_WORDS),
        .ADDR_BITS     (ADDR_BITS),
        .TEMP_MIN      (TEMP_MIN),
        .TEMP_SHIFT    (TEMP_SHIFT)
    ) spi_rx_inst (
        .rst_n          (rst_n),

        .video_sck      (vigil_sck),
        .video_csb      (vigil_csb),
        .video_mosi     (vigil_mosi),

        .wr_allow       (wr_allow),

        .pix_valid      (wr_valid),
        .pix_addr       (wr_addr),
        .pix_data       (wr_data),      
        .frame_done     (wr_frame_done)
    );

    // ========================================================================
    // 2. Double framebuffer with two Gowin_SDP RAMs
    // ========================================================================

    double_framebuffer_gowin_sdp #(
        .FRAME_PIX     (FRAME_PIX),
        .ADDR_BITS     (ADDR_BITS)
        //.RAM_ADDR_BITS (RAM_ADDR_BITS)
    ) double_fb_inst (
        .rst_n          (rst_n),

        // Write side - VIGIL80/SPI clock domain
        .wr_clk         (vigil_sck),       //clock camera IR (4.6 Mbits/s)
        .wr_valid       (wr_valid),        //high when the pixel is ready to be memorized
        .wr_addr        (wr_addr),
        .wr_data        (wr_data),
        .wr_frame_done  (wr_frame_done),   //high when the frame is completed -> swap frambuffer
        .wr_allow       (wr_allow),        //high when the frame received should be saved

        // Read side - HDMI pixel clock domain
        .rd_clk         (rd_clk),
        .rd_swap_point  (rd_swap_point),   //high when the framebuffer needs to be updated
        .rd_req         (rd_req),
        .rd_addr        (rd_addr),
        .rd_data        (rd_pixel),
        .rd_valid       (rd_valid),

        .frame_available(frame_available)
    );

endmodule

// ============================================================================
// MODULE: vigil80_spi_receiver_16to8
// DESCRIPTION:
// Receives VIGIL80 SPI video stream.
//
// VIGIL80 is SPI master:
// - video_sck  generated by camera
// - video_csb  active low, one chip select per frame
// - video_mosi data from camera to FPGA
//
// The first FRAME_PIX words are active image pixels.
// Footer words are discarded.
//
// Each input pixel is 16-bit thermal data.
// Output pixel is 8-bit grayscale.
// ============================================================================

module vigil80_spi_receiver_16to8 #(
    parameter int FRAME_PIX    = 6400,
    parameter int FOOTER_WORDS = 23,
    parameter int TOTAL_WORDS  = FRAME_PIX + FOOTER_WORDS,
    parameter int ADDR_BITS    = $clog2(FRAME_PIX),

    parameter int TEMP_MIN     = 16'd27315,   //Minimum thermal value used as reference for the conversion
    parameter int unsigned TEMP_SHIFT   = 5
)(
    input  logic rst_n,

    input  logic video_sck,   //clock camera IR (4.6 Mbits/s)
    input  logic video_csb,   //chip select active low
    input  logic video_mosi,  //data

    input  logic wr_allow,  //(1: save frame; 0: discard frame)

    output logic pix_valid,    //high when conversion 16 to 8 bit is completed
    output logic [ADDR_BITS-1:0] pix_addr,
    output logic [7:0] pix_data,
    output logic frame_done    //high when the full frame (6400+23 words) is received and must be saved in memory
);

    localparam int WORD_CNT_BITS = $clog2(TOTAL_WORDS);

    logic [15:0] shift_reg_current_word;  //shift register to build up the 16 bits word
    logic [3:0]  bit_cnt;                 //to count from 0 to 15

    logic [WORD_CNT_BITS-1:0] word_cnt;   //Count how many 16-bit words have been received in the current frame

    logic frame_active;       // high while CS frame reception is active
    logic capture_enable;     //useful for preventing wr_allow change while saving 

    // =========================================================================
    // 16-bit thermal value to 8-bit grayscale conversion
    //
    // gray = clamp((thermal - TEMP_MIN) >> TEMP_SHIFT)
    //
    // TEMP_MIN and TEMP_SHIFT can be tuned to improve image contrast.
    // =========================================================================

    function automatic logic [7:0] thermal16_to_gray8(input logic [15:0] thermal);  
        logic [15:0] diff;
        logic [15:0] scaled;
        begin
            if (thermal <= TEMP_MIN) begin
                thermal16_to_gray8 = 8'd0;  //Anything < 0 °C is displayed as black
            end 
            else begin
                diff   = {1'b0, thermal} - {1'b0, TEMP_MIN};
                scaled = diff >> TEMP_SHIFT;

                if (scaled > 16'd255)
                    thermal16_to_gray8 = 8'd255;
                else
                    thermal16_to_gray8 = scaled[7:0];
            end
        end
    endfunction

    // =========================================================================
    // SPI receiver
    // =========================================================================
    logic [15:0] completed_word;   // Word completed by the bit sampled on the current rising SCK edge
    assign completed_word = {shift_reg_current_word[14:0], video_mosi};

always @(posedge video_sck or posedge video_csb or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        shift_reg_current_word <= 16'd0;
        bit_cnt                <= 4'd0;
        word_cnt               <= '0;

        frame_active           <= 1'b0;
        capture_enable         <= 1'b0;

        pix_valid              <= 1'b0;
        pix_addr               <= '0;
        pix_data               <= 8'd0;
        frame_done             <= 1'b0;
    end
    else if (video_csb) begin
        // CSB high terminates the current SPI frame.
        // Realign the receiver immediately, without waiting
        // for an additional video_sck edge.
        shift_reg_current_word <= 16'd0;
        bit_cnt                <= 4'd0;
        word_cnt               <= '0;

        frame_active           <= 1'b0;
        capture_enable         <= 1'b0;

        pix_valid              <= 1'b0;
        frame_done             <= 1'b0;
    end
    else begin
        // Default values: one-clock pulses.
        pix_valid  <= 1'b0;
        frame_done <= 1'b0;

        if (!frame_active) begin
            // First sampled bit of a new SPI frame.
            //
            // VIGIL80 uses:
            // CPOL = 1
            // CPHA = 1
            // MSB first
            //
            // Data is therefore sampled on the rising edge.
            frame_active   <= 1'b1;
            capture_enable <= wr_allow;

            shift_reg_current_word <= {15'd0, video_mosi};

            bit_cnt  <= 4'd1;
            word_cnt <= '0;
        end
        else begin
            // Shift the current serial bit into the word.
            shift_reg_current_word <= {
                shift_reg_current_word[14:0],
                video_mosi
            };

            if (bit_cnt == 4'd15) begin
                // The current 16-bit word is complete.
                bit_cnt <= 4'd0;

                // Only the first 6400 words are image pixels.
                if (capture_enable && (word_cnt < FRAME_PIX)) begin
                    pix_valid <= 1'b1;
                    pix_addr  <= word_cnt[ADDR_BITS-1:0];

                    pix_data <= thermal16_to_gray8(completed_word);
                    //pix_data <= completed_word[15:8];
                end

                // The framebuffer is complete immediately after
                // receiving the last active image pixel.
                //
                // Do not wait for the 23 footer words before
                // notifying the double framebuffer.
                if (capture_enable &&
                    (word_cnt == FRAME_PIX - 1)) begin

                    frame_done <= 1'b1;
                end

                // Continue receiving and discarding the footer
                // in order to preserve frame alignment.
                if (word_cnt == TOTAL_WORDS - 1) begin
                    word_cnt     <= '0;
                    frame_active <= 1'b0;
                end
                else begin
                    word_cnt <= word_cnt + 1'b1;
                end
            end
            else begin
                bit_cnt <= bit_cnt + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end
end
endmodule

// ============================================================================
// MODULE: thermal_hdmi_renderer
// DESCRIPTION:
// Reads 8-bit grayscale pixels from the IR framebuffer and converts them to RGB888.
//
// It scales IMG_W x IMG_H to IMG_W*SCALE x IMG_H*SCALE.
// ============================================================================

module thermal_hdmi_renderer #(
    parameter int H_ACTIVE  = 640,
    parameter int V_ACTIVE  = 480,

    parameter int H_BITS    = $clog2(H_ACTIVE),
    parameter int V_BITS    = $clog2(V_ACTIVE),

    parameter int IMG_W     = 80,
    parameter int IMG_H     = 80,
    parameter int SCALE     = 6,  //Each pixel in the camera will be replicated 6 times vertically and 6 times horizontally
    
    parameter int FRAME_PIX = IMG_W * IMG_H,
    parameter int ADDR_BITS = $clog2(FRAME_PIX)
)(
    input  logic clk_pixel,
    input  logic rst_n,

    input  logic [H_BITS-1:0] cx,
    input  logic [V_BITS-1:0] cy,
    input  logic vde,

    // Read interface from framebuffer to IR manager
    output logic rd_req,
    output logic [ADDR_BITS-1:0] rd_addr,
    input  logic [7:0] rd_pixel,
    input  logic rd_valid,

    // RGB output to TMDS encoder
    output logic [7:0] red,
    output logic [7:0] green,
    output logic [7:0] blue
);


    // ============================================================================
// 8-bit thermal value to RGB thermal palette
//
// Palette:
// 0   -> black
// 64  -> red
// 128 -> yellow
// 192 -> yellow/white
// 255 -> white
// ============================================================================

function automatic logic [23:0] thermal_palette(input logic [7:0] pix);
    logic [7:0] x;
    begin
        // Local ramp inside each range: 0,4,8,...252
        x = {pix[5:0], 2'b00};

        case (pix[7:6])

            // 0..63: black -> red
            2'b00: begin
                thermal_palette = {x, 8'd0, 8'd0};
            end

            // 64..127: red -> yellow
            2'b01: begin
                thermal_palette = {8'hFF, x, 8'd0};
            end

            // 128..191: yellow -> white
            2'b10: begin
                thermal_palette = {8'hFF, 8'hFF, x};
            end

            // 192..255: white
            default: begin
                thermal_palette = {8'hFF, 8'hFF, 8'hFF};
            end

        endcase
    end
endfunction

    // =========================================================================
    // Display dimensions after scaling
    // =========================================================================
    localparam int DISP_W = IMG_W * SCALE;   //480
    localparam int DISP_H = IMG_H * SCALE;   //480

    // =========================================================================
    // Center image on screen
    // =========================================================================
    localparam int X_OFF = (H_ACTIVE - DISP_W) / 2;
    localparam int Y_OFF = (V_ACTIVE - DISP_H) / 2;

    //cx = 0 ----------------------------- 639
    //     80 px      480 px        80 px
    //    +--------+-------------+--------+
    //    | nero   | immagine IR | nero   |
    //    +--------+-------------+--------+
    //     0      79            559      639

    // =========================================================================
    // Source image coordinates
    // =========================================================================
    
    logic in_image_area;    // high within the camera’s valid image area
    logic in_image_area_d;  // signal delayed by 1 clock cycle because SDP RAM is synchronous

    // camera pixels that we want to read
    logic [$clog2(IMG_W)-1:0] src_x;
    logic [$clog2(IMG_H)-1:0] src_y;

    // =========================================================================
    // Generate framebuffer read address
    // =========================================================================

    always_comb begin
        //default values
        in_image_area = 1'b0;
        src_x         = '0;
        src_y         = '0;

        rd_req        = 1'b0;   //don’t read from RAM
        rd_addr       = '0;

        if (vde &&
            (cx >= X_OFF) && (cx < X_OFF + DISP_W) &&
            (cy >= Y_OFF) && (cy < Y_OFF + DISP_H)) begin

            in_image_area = 1'b1;

            //Conversion of HDMI coordinates to camera coordinates
            src_x = (cx - X_OFF) / SCALE;
            src_y = (cy - Y_OFF) / SCALE;

            rd_req  = 1'b1;
            rd_addr = (src_y * IMG_W) + src_x;
        end
    end

    // =========================================================================
    // RAM has one clock latency.
    // Delay image-area flag and then output grayscale as RGB.
    // =========================================================================

    always_ff @(posedge clk_pixel or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            in_image_area_d <= 1'b0;

            red   <= 8'd0;
            green <= 8'd0;
            blue  <= 8'd0;
        end 
        else begin
            in_image_area_d <= in_image_area;

            if (in_image_area_d && rd_valid) begin
                //red   <= rd_pixel;
                //green <= rd_pixel;
                //blue  <= rd_pixel;
                {red, green, blue} <= thermal_palette(rd_pixel);
            end 
            else begin  //out of image : black
                red   <= 8'd0;
                green <= 8'd0;
                blue  <= 8'd0;
            end
        end
    end

endmodule
